chunks: I have seen your flight and your dispersal from the lines,

You were surrounded by rude and low people and Bedouins of Syria (ash-Shām), although you are the chiefs of Arabs and summit of distinction, and possess dignity as that of high nose and big hump of camel.
The sigh of my bosom can subside only when I eventually see you surrounding them as they surrounded you, and see you dislodging them from their position as they dislodged you,

killing them with arrows and striking them with spears so that their forward rows might fall on the rear ones just like the thirsty camels who have been turned away from their places of drink and removed from their water-points.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali describe the dynamics of the Battle of Siffin in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) vividly contrasts the elite status of the Syrian forces ('yamā'if al-sharaf') with their actual composition of 'al-jufāt al-ṭaghām' (the rough and uncouth), highlighting the irony of their defeat by commoners. He expresses deep personal satisfaction in witnessing their humiliation, using the powerful metaphor of thirsty camels driven from their water sources to illustrate their displacement and loss of dignity. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly view that true nobility lies in piety and leadership rather than mere tribal lineage, a theme central to the narrative of Siffin.
